raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose
Add eager break for Mamba-family ops under breakable CUDA graphs

Ops listed in `CompilationConfig._attention_ops` are excluded from CUDA graphs via FX graph splitting. That only works under `torch.compile`.

This PR applys these splitting into breakable cudagraph.

## Test Plan
nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 on PRO5000
```bash

# server
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server --model nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16  --port 8123 --host localhost --trust-remote-code --gpu-memory-util=0.9 --max-num-batched-tokens=4096      -tp=4
# client
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --task gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 --model_args "model=nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16,base_url=http://localhost:8123/v1/chat/completions,max_gen_toks=4096,num_concurrent=64,timeout=5000,max_retries=5" --apply_chat_template --output_path ./lm_eval_output --log_samples
```

before this pr:

```
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

after this pr:

```
|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr|
|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9507|±  |0.0060|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9416|±  |0.0065|
```

## Test Result

- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.

</details>

> Why we need to add this?

With `torch.compile` + PIECEWISE, ops in `CompilationConfig._attention_ops` (including `mamba_mixer`, `mamba_mixer2`, `short_conv`, `linear_attention`, `olmo_hybrid_gdn_full_forward`) are used as splitting ops, so they run eagerly outside the cudagraph.

Under breakable graph, these ops will be captured, causing mamba models failure issues. This PR adds `@eager_break_during_capture` to these ops so the breakable path matches the existing PIECEWISE behavior.

nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 on PRO5000
```bash

# server
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server --model nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16  --port 8123 --host localhost --trust-remote-code --gpu-memory-util=0.9 --max-num-batched-tokens=4096      -tp=4
# client

```


after this pr:

```

|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9507|±  |0.0060|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9416|±  |0.0065|
```

My point is that this isn't a bug that arises from real-world usage

let me illustrate some background for XPU: we want to make breakable graph to default (or recommended config) on XPU
1. for legacy models, it's easier to track performance, we can ignore noise from compile based approach( like performance regression). 
2. for new modes, it's aligned with cuda new modeling design.

> for new modes, it's aligned with cuda new modeling design.

new models should go to `vllm/models`
